title: One Ångström From 959 Worm Cells to Rewound Pluripotency — C. elegans 1,090 -> 959 Lineage & egl-1/ced-9/ced-4/ced-3 Suicide Switch (PDB 2A5Y, 3LQQ, 3JBT), Gurdon's Nuclear Transfer, Yamanaka's 24 -> 4 OSKM Subtraction & OCT4–SOX2 Prying DNA 7 Å Off the Nucleosome (PDB 6T90)

teenKit.tldr: Your body relies on a constant, silent wave of programmed cell suicide to keep you alive, and scientists discovered how to reverse this timeline to turn adult cells back into embryonic blank slates.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how cells choose to die or reset their age is the foundation for curing cancer and regenerating damaged human tissues.
keyTakeaways: Right now, about 700,000 of your cells are actively executing a programmed suicide every second, which is essential for your survival.
Cellular suicide is controlled by a precise molecular switch network involving genes like egl-1, ced-9, ced-4, and ced-3.
Scientists can rewind specialized adult cells back to an embryonic state using just four transcription factors known as the OSKM cocktail.

vocab.meaning: The body's process of programmed cell death that cleans up damaged or unneeded cells without causing inflammation.
A tiny transparent nematode roundworm used by scientists to map exact cell lineages and death pathways.
The biological state of an immature stem cell that has the potential to turn into any cell type in the body.
A structural unit of a DNA strand wrapped around histone protein cores, acting like spools to pack genetic material.

quiz.question: What would happen if your cells suddenly stopped undergoing programmed cell death (apoptosis)?
options: You would instantly gain superhuman regeneration abilities.
Your cells would live forever and you wouldn't survive the week.
Your body would stop producing energy.
Nothing at all would change in your daily life.
quiz.explanation: Apoptosis is vital for removing dangerous or unneeded cells; without it, tissues malfunction and life cannot be sustained.

quiz.question: How many transcription factors did Shinya Yamanaka ultimately use to reprogram adult cells back to pluripotency (the OSKM cocktail)?
quiz.explanation: Yamanaka famously screened down a list of 24 candidate genes until he isolated the crucial 4 OSKM factors required for reprogramming.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of the OCT4-SOX2 protein complex when interacting with DNA?
options: It cuts DNA into tiny fragments for cellular recycling.
It physically pries DNA about 7 angstroms off the nucleosome spool.
It glues different chromosomes together to form a nucleus.
It destroys ribosomes to halt protein production.
quiz.explanation: OCT4 and SOX2 act as pioneer factors that physically peel tightly wound DNA off its histone spools to access locked-away genes.
